steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C). Line a cookie sheet with parchment paper.

Mix sugar and oil together in a large bowl until well blended. Mix in vanilla and almond extracts, then beat in eggs. Combine flour, baking powder, and salt in a separate bowl; gradually stir into egg mixture until combined. Fold in pistachios and cranberries by hand.
Divide dough in half. Form each piece into a 12x2-inch log on the prepared cookie sheet. Dough may be sticky; wet hands with cool water to handle dough more easily.
Bake in the preheated oven until logs are light brown, about 35 minutes. Remove from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes.
Reduce oven temperature to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C).
Cut logs on the diagonal into 3/4-inch-thick slices. Lay cookies cut-side down on the cookie sheet.
Bake cookies until dry, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Cranberry Pistachio Biscotti
raw_recipe.description: These cranberry pistachio biscotti made with juicy red cranberries and crunchy green pistachios make a colorful and festive holiday cookie.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make special biscotti with the traditional red and green colors of the holiday. Just make sure you make enough, as these will be the hit of your holiday party.

review.reviewBody:
This is perhaps the most fantastic cookie I have ever made in my life.

Here are my tips:

1) I used 1/2 the amount of dried cranberries (actually used orange crasins)

2) I used 1 tsp. of orange zest and added it right into the batter (next time I am upping this to 1 tablespoon)

3) I used slivered almonds instead of the pistachio nuts. The slivered almonds worked very well because they did not "chunk up" the batter.

4) When I took the loaves out of the oven, I immediately covered them with two dishtowels so that the loaves would cool more slowly. It's the sudden change in temperature that makes things out of the oven "crack" on top, and the dishtowels minimized this. 

5) I transferred one loaf at a time to my wooden cutting board and cut diagonal slices with a large bread knife. I did now saw. I simply leaned into it with my body weight, and all my slices came out pretty cleanly. I also first cut off just a tad bit from either in at first before cutting the slices off.

6) I melted white chocolate in the microwave and dipped on end in, then sprinkled with red and green colored sugars. 
By doing all of this, (oh, plus you MUST wet your fingertips while working with the dough before it goes in the oven), I got 24 clean slices. These freeze beautifully as well. I LOVE this recipe!

This is a wonderful recipe. Italian friends have told me this taste "just the way biscotti is supposed to taste." I reduced pistachios by 1/2 cup and increased the cranberries by 1/2 cup. I also add 1/2 tsp. real orange extract. Otherwise, the recipe is perfect. If you are not getting 3 dozen, you may be making the logs too wide. Make them 2 inches wide and then flatten them slighty. It is a smaller biscotti than those sold in jars at coffee shops. DON'T use butter or margarine. Find a light good quality olive oil. Butter doesn't belong in biscotti--it won't age well and will become rancid instead of allowing the flavor to develop.

By gads! This is the very =best= biscotti recipe! Usually I can't stand those nasty little bricks, but these are delicious! Try these even if you usually don't like biscotti... m-m-m-m yummy. HINT: Use a regular knife to cut these... the serrated blade makes a big mess.

I made these biscotti for the holidays because they are apparently a popular holiday item. I think the biscotti turned out just okay. I am 100% Italian-American and an exceptional Italian cook. I grew up cooking and baking with my beloved mom and I've made MANY biscotti in my lifetime. After reviewing similar recipes, I made some simple changes to this recipe because I think doing so makes the biscotti a bit more authentic & tasty. For starters, I increased my oven temp to 325F degrees; you might also do 350F degrees, a standard temp for biscotti. I increased the flour to 2-2 1/4 cups, added 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tsp orange extract & 1/4 tsp of cinnamon. I changed the olive oil to 1/3 c vegetable oil 'cause I think olive oil is way too heavy for biscotti. I also added even cups of dried cranberries and pistachios. I ALWAYS bake biscotti on parchment paper! As the biscotti cooled, I melted 8 ounces of semi-sweet chocolate with 1 tsp of shortening and when melted, dipped the biscotti into the mixture. I think without a chocolate glaze, the biscotti are way too bland...I think chocolate makes the biscuits a LOT more interesting. Finally, if you are into baking biscotti like I am, invest in a simple electric knife for cutting the logs...it really is the only way to go! Also, forget all the flipping and turning. Simply cut your biscotti while warm, space them a bit, keep them upright & return them to the oven for another 15-20 minutes. Enjoy and happy baking!

This has become my "go-to" biscotti recipe. It can't fail. I've made it many times with great success. I did make some changes: increased flour to 2 cups (because the dough was too soft and spread out too much), and used 1 cup pistachios, and 1 cup of cranberries. Also tried substituting 1/4 cup dark brown sugar for 1/4 cup of the white sugar, and adding 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips and 1 cup of chopped walnuts. Delish! Tasted like a "Toll House" biscotti. Just recently I tried something new - replaced 1/2 cup of the flour with 1/2 cup Dutch-processed cocoa, used 1 tablespoon Frangelico (hazelnut liquor)and 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla instead of the usual amount of vanilla and almond extracts and folded in 1 cup toasted hazelnuts and 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips - excellent Chocolate/Hazelnut biscotti. I use an ice cream scoop to place the dough on the cookie sheets and then just use my spatula to join the scoops together. No more sticky hands!

This recipe is an absolute winner. It's super easy to make and it's delicious. I've been making it every Christmas now for 3 years and friends/family are now requesting it in advance. 

Some observations from my own experience:

1) it is VERY sticky. the recipe says to mix the cranberries and pistachio in with your hands but I used a spatula and found it much easier. It also helped when I split the dough in half in the bowl and transferred it to the silicon sheet/parchment paper on the cookie sheet to form the logs. I was able to use nearly all of the dough using this method, too, because I didn't have as much stuck to my hands.

2) After the 1st baking phase and after allowing the logs to rest for 10 min, I carefully transferred the logs to a cutting board to avoid tearing/cutting the parchment paper/silicon.

3) This year, I ran low on pistachios and had a lot of cranberries so I matched the amount to 1 cup each instead of 1.5 c pistachios and .5 cup cranberries. I will likely do that again as it turned out very well with more sweetness and still the lovely pistachio flavor/appearance.

4) After the 2nd bake time, I turn the oven off and leave the completed biscotti in it as it cools. This gives it an additional bit of crunch without the rock hard texture that store-bought biscotti often has.

Excellent recipe! Made it the first time AS WRITTEN. You Definitely have to keep stirring, so it doesn’t burn, keep the flame very low! Sugar/honey will carmelize and get darker if heated too high too fast. Unfortunately my torrone, like many others, was delicious, but came out beige, not white as I had expected. So the 2nd round, I followed everything again EXCEPT for exchanging the honey with light corn syrup and adding 3 beaten egg whites instead of 2. BINGO! Light, bright and perfect! No taste difference in not having honey flavor. I did both times use a heavy cast iron/porcelain Dutch oven, which on low, keeps the heat even. Yes this requires a lot of stirring, but SO worth it, especially if you want to cut these into logs, wrap in brown butcher paper, twine and decorative holly - perfect gift to give out to friends, neighbors and family!!

These biscotti are a great addition to my collection of cookie recipes. I did follow some advice given by Toni Lee who suggested using 1/3 cup canola oil instead of olive oil and increasing flour to 2 cups. She also replaces 1 tsp vanilla with 1 tsp of orange extract and adds 1/4 tsp cinnamon. I baked them at 325 for 35 min then sliced with an electric knife before putting them back in the oven for 8 min. I still had some breakage when I sliced them, but I think that’s hard to avoid with all the nuts and craisins in them. 

I do have one suggestion that will be very helpful concerning mixing and shaping with your hands. I used a vinyl glove like the ones everyone has bought because of the pandemic. I had absolutely no sticking to my hands AT ALL! Try it!

These are almost the same as my recipe that I’ve used for years. Difference is, I use butter instead of olive oil and add crushed anise seed. I also dip them in white chocolate. Always made a double batch since they are friends favorite.

After reading several reviews here, I did follow directions as written with a few modifications as follows: NUTS: used 1/2 Cup salted pistachios, 1/2 Cup plain Hazelnuts and 1/2 Cup plain Pumpkin Seeds. I soaked 1/2 Cup of dried Cranberries in 1/2 Cup very warm filtered water and let it sit about an hour. I drained all the liquid before adding to the dough. I think it would be best to warn First Time Bakers of how very sloppy the dough is. It scared me. I plopped the mixture out, giant spoonful by spoonful onto my parchment , lined cookies sheet in two "strips" as even as possible. To my OCD self, these were sloppy enough to cause great anxiety. I WET MY HANDS AS INSTRUCTED and quickly and carefully smoothed out the two sloppy cow pucky plops to the best of my ability. I said a swift prayer and carefully slid them into the oven. Using this ancient 60 year old Hardwick Gas Stove, I set my timer for seventeen minutes and turned the baking tray completely around and baked an additional 17 minutes. I did wait the ten minutes before pushing the blade down evenly to slice 3/4 inches on a diagonal and ate the ends ! Oh my goodness !!! DELICIOUS !!!
Best biscotti I’ve ever made. Tweaked a little . Needed another heaping 1/4 cup of flour. Also after cutting, I baked the cut side 7 minutes, flipped, baked the other side another 7 minutes
These really turned out nice! They weren't real dry and crunchy like store-bought biscotti. They were flavorful and chewy and we just loved them!
Excellent recipe. Sometimes I dip a third of the cookie in melted chocolate for a extra burst of sweetness.
Easy for anyone
Agree with other reviewers that cooking time and/or temperature is off. Also agree on way too many nuts. Taste ok but not great. I’ll be using a different recipe from now on.
Nice and easy. 2nd time making them. I put fresh lemon zest as I don’t have almond extract. They turn out great!
Delicious
Used costco shelled pistachios, so left out added salt. Printed it to keep forever. A perfect biscotti recipe.
Mixed the dough a little too long the first time so the dough really spread out. Still GREAT flavor and crunch. Just made another batch…these are easy and addictive!

I made these last night and watched the video on how to cut them. There is no way to get 36 biscotti if you cut them lengthwise as they did in the video. They also didn't make the logs 2 x 24. If you follow the instructions, and cut them the opposite way, you can get 36. I made them slightly thicker and got 30. Of course you can add any flavorings like orange or cinnamon or cardamom to spice them up. You can also use different nuts. I used avocado oil instead of olive and they held together nicely. I did the initial bake for 35 minutes, let them sit covered for 8 and then baked them at 275 for 30 minutes. Then I turned the oven off and kept them in the closed oven until they were cool. They came out perfectly toasted and crisp. They held together and are flavorful. Next time I am going to use melted butter and add some orange zest and extract.
